purpose: Recurring MicroDuck faults: every occurrence, the hypotheses and the tests that separate them, what is only a mitigation, and whether each lost function comes back by itself. Rule: ~/code/claude-config/rules/common/recurring-fault-cause-first.md. Check: python3 microduck-sim/faults_check.py (fails while a repeated fault has no confirmed cause and no test run or queued with its blocker, or while a lost function is not shown to recover after an induced fault).

touch-twi0-jam.symptom: The head touch bus (TWI0 2510000.twi, XIAO ESP32-S3 slave 0x2A, A7Z pins 29/31) stops answering: the XIAO acks its address, every read stalls after the first data byte (kernel 'TWI BUS error state is 0x50', 'bus state 0xf9, isn't idle', 'STOP failed') and the pads stay dead until the duck is powered off.
touch-twi0-jam.required_recovery: The pads come back by themselves, with no power-off and no opening of the head. Shawn 2026-10-31: "另外你说出现问题 触摸板自己不能恢复 只能走路 这个解决方案是完全不能接受的" and "为什么你会觉得这种残疾方案可以接受呢".

occurrences.what: every read shifted by a 0x55 filler byte from about 15 min into run app1029-195814c, with 'ACK not received' in dmesg (CURRENT-STATE a7z_touch_bus); the same fault family, not yet a jam

occurrences.what: induced under T1 condition both (4-channel capture + four busy processes, 50 Hz reads, app telemetry 10 Hz) on the original firmware about 2 min in: 'Arbitration lost' (0x38) then 0x50 / STOP failed / bus state 0xf9 for good, the 16:33:35 signature. LCR 0x2a: SDA low, SCL high. With TWI0 unbound SDA stayed low 100 % of 1 s: the XIAO holds it. The XIAO loop kept running (no reboot). Two SCL clocks from the A7Z released SDA; after a STOP 10 of 10 reads were good

hypotheses.claim: Weak pull-ups on a long bundle: only the chips' internal pull-ups (typical about 100 k on the A7Z, 45 k on the XIAO) on wires running from the head down the neck to the saddle (D-022) next to the amplifier I2S lines and, since 10/29, the microphone I2S lines (BCLK about 3 MHz while capturing). Edges too slow plus crosstalk corrupt a bit; the slave loses step.
hypotheses.for: the fault family appears 10/29, the day all three microphones were fitted and capture began; the jammed boots ran namecall's capture; 10/21 in the head with short wires: 611 reads, 0 lost
hypotheses.against: not measured: rise time and the bundle route are estimates

hypotheses.claim: CPU load (namecall 200-400 %) delays the TWI interrupt between bytes; a long mid-read pause trips the ESP32 slave's own timeout, which resets its state while the master continues, so the two lose step.
hypotheses.for: all recorded jams with namecall running
hypotheses.against: 2026-10-31 19:12, twi0_induce.py --pause-ms (stretch-aware bit-banged master, SCL held low mid-read, then the read finished): pauses of 5, 50, 500 and 3000 ms, 3 trials each, every block read correctly and every later kernel read fine
hypotheses.status: ruled out as a single-event trigger

hypotheses.claim: touch_main.cpp builds the reply inside onRequest with interrupts off and has no timeout or watchdog: once its TX buffer is out of step (the 10/29 filler shift) it stretches SCL on every read and never recovers.
hypotheses.for: the stall after the first data byte with the address still acked; the jam lasts until power-off; the 10/29 misalignment: reproduced 2026-10-31 19:05 by one 32-byte read of the 24-byte block (every later read starts with 0x55 and is shifted one byte; it stays shifted, RS realigns it, the brain's parser accepts the shift)
hypotheses.against: 2026-10-31 19:15 on the original firmware (1d8a9d03, same core 3.3.12): aborted reads (4), one extra SCL edge mid-read (6), a false START/STOP mid-read (6) and an over-read each left the bus answering at once; the lasting stall was not reproduced by any single event
hypotheses.status: open: persistence not reproduced by single events; T1 running

tests.what: twi0_jam_test.py on the A7Z: 5 min per condition, reads at the brain's rate: (a) nothing else running, (b) microphone capture only, (c) CPU load only, (d) both; counts TWI0 kernel errors, failed reads and wedges, and records the line state (TWI_LCR) at each wedge. H1 predicts (b) and (d) fail; H2 predicts (c) and (d); neither: firmware only.
tests.results: 2026-10-31 20:03:30-20:11:30 (twi0_cells_test.py, brain in stand as the only reader, new firmware): capture off / hands off 0 events; capture off / grip 0; capture on / grip 5 events (20:08:06, 08:31, 08:47, 08:51, 09:24: STOP failed with bus 0xf9, or address NACK); capture on / hands off 2 (20:09:46, 20:10:37; Shawn released late, so part of this cell was still gripped). No event lasted: every one ended at once. Capture is necessary in this session: 0 of 7 events without it (4 min + the 37 s grip at 19:28); the hand raises the rate but is not separated.
tests.runs: with the running brain as the only reader (twi0_jam_test.py watch mode counts kernel onsets): capture on / off x hand on head / off, 2 min each; H1 with hand coupling predicts onsets only in capture + hand. Done so far: both (capture + load) reproduced the jam at 19:19:14; capture alone 5 min: 0 onsets; capture + hand + brain 2.7 min: 3 onsets; hand alone: 0

tests.what: induce wedges and measure the time until reads return without a power-off
tests.results: 2026-10-31 19:08-19:10, twi0_hold_test.py (XIAO holds SDA or SCL low on HD/HC, as a slave out of step does; 50 Hz reads through the bound kernel driver, nothing rebound): line watchdog paused (RD): SDA 16.9 s and 16.8 s, SCL 16.9 s stuck until the window ended; line watchdog on: SDA 5 of 5 and SCL 5 of 5 back in 0.02-0.16 s with one to seven failed reads, the kernel driver recovering by itself. Shifted reads (H3): RS realigns at once. Not covered yet: the real jam's own state, until T1 reproduces it.

mitigations: console loglevel 1 (2026-10-31 17:12): the kernel's error lines no longer starve the servo UART; 17:20 jam: brain 47 Hz, 3 of 1500 ticks missing
walk_wired.py parser length and CRC checks (bb9e9b06), touch back-off (cc0593d7), app telemetry back-off (microduck-simulator 8439ab6)

recovery.evidence: the real jam state is the XIAO holding SDA (19:19-19:27, unbound probe); the same state injected from the XIAO (HD) recovers in 0.02-0.16 s, 8 of 8 incl. 19:28 after the final flash; three real onsets on b0056 (19:46:23, 19:46:37, 19:46:43 A7Z clock: 'Arbitration lost' then 0x50 / STOP failed) each ended within 0.19 s with no power-off, and the running brain (app1031-194539, stand, new walk_wired.py) kept reading touch ('reads back' after every failure). Cold boot with the USB out: 25 of 25 reads. Recovered functions only; the onset stays open under cause.
recovery.plan: touch_main.cpp: once the bus has been idle, a line held low 30 ms restarts the whole XIAO; Wire.begin is retried every 100 ms until it succeeds; task watchdog; RS restart, RD pause and HD/HC hold commands; serial never blocks. walk_wired.py sends RS after 10 failed reads. Firmware bugs found and fixed 2026-10-31 while testing it: (1) the core's slave init refuses to start while a line is low and never retries, so a restart during a held line or during the A7Z's boot left the slave dead (069aec6a and f629c8c0 in the robot; reproduced by holding SCL 200 ms: 0 of 25 reads; fixed: 25 of 25); (2) with USB plugged in and the Mac's port closed each serial write waited 2 s and the task watchdog restarted the XIAO (fixed with setTxTimeoutMs(0), 86f9f7c7). During T1 the XIAO runs the original firmware; the new build is reflashed after it.

cause.summary: microphone capture (I2S clocks beside the touch wires, H1) makes the bit errors, confirmed by capture on/off cells 2026-10-31 20:03-20:11; a hand on the head raises the rate; the lasting jam was the XIAO slave left holding SDA, now cleared by its line watchdog
cause.fix_proposed: stiffen the lines: 2.2 kOhm pull-ups from SDA and SCL to 3V3 at the XIAO (XIAO soldering is allowed, D-013), and/or route the touch pair apart from the I2S wires in the neck; acceptance: twi0_cells_test.py capture-on cells with 0 events. Deferred by Shawn 2026-10-31 20:1x until the head is next opened ("又要开颅 肯定要以后了"); touch self-recovers meanwhile.
cause.evidence: Mechanism (19:19-19:27): a bit error on the line (first error always 'Arbitration lost') leaves the XIAO's slave a few bits out of step, driving SDA low and waiting for clocks; the sunxi driver never clocks it out, so the jam lasts until power-off. Onset: all three jammed boots had microphone capture running 2-6 min before the jam (16:30:18 -> 16:33:35, 17:11:30 -> 17:17:40, 19:17 -> 19:19:14); 16:58-17:11 without capture read fine. Shawn's hand on the head (19:28:50-19:29:27, pads 23.6k -> 30.5k, A7Z idle) gave 0 errors; mid-read pauses up to 3 s gave none (H2 ruled out). Capture alone (19:39:03-19:44:10 A7Z clock, arecord 4 ch + aplay keepalive, no brain, new firmware): 0 kernel errors in 5 min, one byte-shift at 19:42:09 (Shawn was hot-gluing the microphone backs in the head that hour). Then 19:44:22-19:47:05 another session's snap-test capture with Shawn's hands at the head (pads to 31k at 19:45:45) and, from 19:45:39, a brain in stand with torque on: 3 full onsets and 5 short ACK/STOP errors. Hand alone (no capture, no brain): 0. So no single factor triggers it here; capture with a hand at the head and/or a running brain does. Separating test queued in T1.

spin-stall-fixed-heading.symptom: A turn in place (vtheta +-0.5) steps but stops gaining heading at a fixed heading and springs back about 20 deg when the command stops; approach ends with 'not following the right arc', and its 'facing it' reading turns into a bearing about 20 deg off after the spring-back.
spin-stall-fixed-heading.required_recovery: The duck turns in place to any bearing the flow asks for. Shawn 2026-11-01: test the full flow, find, walk and pick.

head-camera-usb-drop.symptom: The U20CAM leaves USB bus 1 during turning; enumeration fails with error -71 and a controller rebind does not bring it back, so seepick has no picture.
head-camera-usb-drop.required_recovery: The camera comes back by itself or the connection stops dropping.

occurrences.what: 'usb 1-1: USB disconnect', then 'new full-speed', 'device descriptor read/64, error -71' twice, then nothing; xhci unbind/bind at 21:40 finds no device
occurrences.running: turn_test right spin nearing the -50 deg stall, a7z_cam daemon streaming

hypotheses.claim: The camera's USB-C plug at the A7Z lost contact: the Type-C chip read CC1 and CC2 Open at 21:37:54, the same second as the disconnect, so VBUS went off and a controller rebind could not bring it back.
hypotheses.status: supported: Shawn re-plugged it and at 21:43:15 CC1 read Rd and the camera enumerated at high speed; what moved the plug is not known

tests.what: Re-plug the USB-C plug, then lsusb and a fresh frame

recovery.evidence: needs a re-plug by hand; xhci rebind did not recover it (21:40), re-plug did (21:43)

cause.summary: USB-C plug contact at the A7Z; one occurrence
